title: Joshua Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 15.

questions.question: What was the uttermost part of the south coast for the tribe of Judah?
options: The border of Edom, the wilderness of Zin
questions.correctAnswer: The border of Edom, the wilderness of Zin
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:1 states that the uttermost part of the south coast was the border of Edom, the wilderness of Zin.

questions.question: From where did the south border of Judah start according to Joshua 15?
options: From the shore of the salt sea
questions.correctAnswer: From the shore of the salt sea
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:2 says that the south border was from the shore of the salt sea, from the bay that looketh southward.

questions.question: Which city was given to Caleb the son of Jephunneh among the children of Judah?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:13 states that Caleb was given the city of Arba, which is Hebron.

questions.question: Who were the three sons of Anak that Caleb drove out of Hebron?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:14 identifies the three sons of Anak as Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, who Caleb drove out.

questions.question: What was the former name of Debir before it was called Debir?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:15 says the name of Debir before was Kirjathsepher.

questions.question: Who took Kirjathsepher and received Achsah as wife?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:17 states that Othniel took Kirjathsepher and was given Achsah as wife.

questions.question: What did Achsah ask her father Caleb for when she came to him?
options: A field with springs of water
questions.correctAnswer: A field with springs of water
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:19 describes Achsah asking her father for springs of water in addition to the south land she had received.

questions.question: True or False: The border of the tribe of Judah included the valley of the son of Hinnom.
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:8 states that the border went up by the valley of the son of Hinnom.

questions.question: True or False: The children of Judah were able to drive out the Jebusites from Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:63 says that the children of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, who dwelt with them in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which sea was the east border of the tribe of Judah?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:5 states that the east border was the salt sea, even unto the end of Jordan.

questions.question: In Joshua 15, which city is also called Baalah?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:9 identifies Baalah as Kirjathjearim.

questions.question: True or False: Caleb promised his daughter Achsah to the man who captured Kirjathsepher.
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:16 states that Caleb said whoever smote Kirjathsepher and took it would receive Achsah as wife.

questions.question: Which border was described as extending to the great sea?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:12 says the west border was to the great sea and the coast thereof.

questions.question: True or False: The border of Judah passed by the stone of Bohan, the son of Reuben.
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:6 says the border went up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben, but it does not say it passed by or included it as part of the border in that manner; the text states it as a boundary point, not passing by as a separate location.

questions.question: In what order do these locations appear on the south border of Judah: Maalehacrabbim, Zin, Kadeshbarnea?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:3 lists the south border as going out to Maalehacrabbim, then passing along to Zin, and ascending to Kadeshbarnea in that order.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Which three sons of Anak did Caleb drive out of Hebron according to Joshua 15?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:14 states that Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak named Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai from Hebron. These were the Anakim giants occupying the city.

questions.question: What promise did Caleb make regarding the city of Kirjathsepher (Debir) as recorded in Joshua 15?
options: He who captures it will marry his daughter Achsah
He who captures it will receive double inheritance
He who captures it will become king of Judah
He who captures it will be made a priest
questions.correctAnswer: He who captures it will marry his daughter Achsah
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:16 explains that Caleb promised his daughter Achsah in marriage to whoever captured Kirjathsepher (Debir). This shows Caleb's encouragement of courage and faithfulness.

questions.question: How does the passage in Joshua 15:18-19 illustrate the virtue of humility and prayer through Achsah's request?
options: Achsah humbly asks for springs of water and receives a blessing
Achsah demands a vast territory without prayer
Achsah refuses gifts and asks for nothing
Achsah prays for Caleb to be king
questions.correctAnswer: Achsah humbly asks for springs of water and receives a blessing
questions.explanation: In Joshua 15:18-19, Achsah humbly asks her father for springs of water after receiving land, demonstrating prayerfulness and recognizing her need. Caleb blesses her with both upper and nether springs, showing God's provision through humility and prayer.

questions.question: Which city was given to Caleb, according to the commandment of the LORD to Joshua?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:13 states that Caleb was given the city of Arba, which is Hebron, as part of the inheritance among the children of Judah according to God's command to Joshua.

questions.question: What does Joshua 15:32 reveal about the cities listed there?
options: They are twenty-nine cities with their villages
They are the only cities in Judah
They are cities conquered by Caleb alone
They are cities outside the tribe of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: They are twenty-nine cities with their villages
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:32 summarizes that the cities mentioned before are twenty-nine in total along with their villages, emphasizing the extent of Judah's inheritance.

questions.question: Which of the following cities is NOT listed among the southern cities of Judah in Joshua 15:21-31?
questions.explanation: Jericho is not listed among the cities of Judah in Joshua 15:21-31. Instead, these verses mention cities like Ziklag, Beersheba, and Dimonah as part of Judah's southern territory.

questions.question: According to Joshua 15:40-41, what quality do the cities Gederoth, Bethdagon, Naamah, and Makkedah share?
options: They are sixteen cities with their villages
They are all located on the sea coast
They belong to the tribe of Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: They are sixteen cities with their villages
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:41 groups Gederoth, Bethdagon, Naamah, and Makkedah among sixteen cities with their villages, highlighting the extent of Judah's settled towns.

questions.question: What does Joshua 15:25 indicate about Hezron in relation to Hazor?
options: Hezron is a river near Hazor
Hezron is a different tribe than Hazor
Hezron is the father of Hazor
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:25 identifies Hezron as which is Hazor, indicating that the city was known by both names, illustrating biblical naming practices.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 15:63, the children of Judah completely drove out the Jebusites from Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:63 clearly states that the children of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, who continued to dwell with them in Jerusalem.

questions.question: How does the listing of cities in Joshua 15:33-36 demonstrate the virtue of diligence in inheritance?
options: It shows the thoroughness in claiming and organizing the land with its villages
It shows negligence as many villages are missing
It reflects only the cities taken by Caleb
It illustrates the failure to capture the promised land
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the thoroughness in claiming and organizing the land with its villages
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:33-36 lists cities along with their villages, showing the careful and diligent effort to claim and organize the land given to Judah, which reflects obedience and faithfulness.

questions.question: Which city is mentioned in Joshua 15:46 as lying near Ashdod and its villages?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:45-46 mentions Ekron along with its towns and villages, and from Ekron to the sea near Ashdod with their villages, showing the western border of Judah.

questions.question: What does the description of the west border in Joshua 15:12 teach about the nature of Judah’s territory?
options: It borders the great sea, offering access to maritime trade
It is landlocked with no access to water
It borders the desert with no resources
It only borders other tribes of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It borders the great sea, offering access to maritime trade
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:12 states the west border of Judah is the great sea (Mediterranean), indicating Judah had access to the sea, which could facilitate trade and resources.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 15:53, Bethtappuah is one of the cities with its villages in the mountains of Judah.
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:53 lists Bethtappuah among other cities in the mountainous region of Judah, confirming its inclusion in the inheritance.

questions.question: In Joshua 15:54-57, what common characteristic do the cities Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah, Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, Cain, Gibeah, and Timnah share?
options: They are all cities with their villages
They are all located on the southern border
They were not conquered by Judah
They are cities of the tribe of Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: They are all cities with their villages
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:54-57 groups these cities together as cities with their villages, emphasizing the structured inheritance and settlement by the tribe of Judah.

questions.question: True or False: The passage in Joshua 15:22-42 mainly focuses on listing the cities and their villages within the tribe of Judah's inheritance.
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:22-42 extensively lists numerous cities and villages belonging to Judah, highlighting the thorough distribution of land among the tribe’s families.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 15.

questions.question: Which city was given to Caleb as an inheritance according to Joshua 15?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:13 states that Caleb was given the city of Arba, the father of Anak, which city is Hebron, as his inheritance.

questions.question: Who was the brother of Caleb that took Kirjathsepher and married Achsah?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:17 tells us that Othniel, Caleb's brother, took Kirjathsepher and married Achsah, Caleb's daughter.

questions.question: What specific request did Achsah make to her father Caleb?
options: A field with springs of water
questions.correctAnswer: A field with springs of water
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:19 explains that Achsah asked Caleb for a blessing and specifically for springs of water in addition to the south land he had given her.

questions.question: Which city is identified as Kirjathjearim in Joshua 15?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:9 indicates that Baalah is another name for Kirjathjearim.

questions.question: Which city is mentioned as not being driven out by the children of Judah, where Jebusites still dwelt?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:63 states that the Jebusites, inhabitants of Jerusalem, were not driven out by the children of Judah and dwelt there to this day.

questions.question: Which river is mentioned as the western border in Joshua 15?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:4 mentions the river of Egypt as the western boundary of the southern border of Judah.

questions.question: Which city in Joshua 15 is also known as Kirjathsannah?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:49 identifies Kirjathsannah as the former name of Debir.

questions.question: How many cities and their villages are listed toward the end of Joshua 15 for the tribe of Judah?
questions.explanation: The combined total of cities and their villages listed from Joshua 15:21 through 15:62 amounts to ninety-six, encompassing the entire inheritance of Judah.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Joshua 15 to organize the extensive listing of cities and borders?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15 uses inclusio by framing the extensive lists of cities and borders with geographical markers and key cities, creating a literary envelope around the inheritance description (Joshua 15:1, 15:63).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament book also details the allotment of land to the tribe of Judah, complementing Joshua 15?
questions.explanation: Numbers 34 and 26 provide earlier descriptions of land allotments and tribal boundaries that are fulfilled and detailed in Joshua 15, showing continuity of God's promise.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'Kirjath' found in many city names in Joshua 15, such as Kirjathsepher and Kirjathjearim?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Kirjath' (קִרְיַת) means 'city' or 'town,' explaining its frequent use as a prefix in place names to denote a settlement, as seen in Joshua 15:15 and 15:60.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 15, the territory of Judah extended from the Great Sea on the west to the Salt Sea on the east.
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:5 and 15:12 describe the east border as the Salt Sea and the west border as the Great Sea, confirming Judah's territory spanned from sea to sea.

questions.question: True or False: The tribe of Judah successfully drove out the inhabitants of Jerusalem according to Joshua 15.
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:63 clearly states that the children of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem, and the Jebusites continued to dwell there.

questions.question: Which city listed in Joshua 15 is associated with a significant prophetic event in the New Testament, where Jesus was anointed by Mary?
questions.explanation: While not explicitly mentioned in Joshua 15, Bethany is near the territory of Judah and is historically significant in the New Testament as the place where Jesus was anointed (John 12), showing continuity of biblical geography and narrative.
questions.verseReference: Joshua 15:59 (Bethanoth as a related name); John 12

questions.question: Which city mentioned in Joshua 15 is known from archaeological findings as a Philistine city, indicating the coexistence or conflict with Judah?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:45-46 mentions Ekron, known historically as a major Philistine city, showing the geopolitical complexities of the region during the period of Israelite settlement.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by the LORD’s allocation of the tribe of Judah’s territory as described in Joshua 15:1?
options: God’s omnipotence in creating the world
God’s omniscience in knowing all things
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:1 details the precise allotment of land to Judah by their families, revealing God's attribute of justice in fairly distributing the inheritance among His people, reflecting His righteous governance (Deuteronomy 32:4).

questions.question: How does the description of the south border extending to the river of Egypt and the great sea (Joshua 15:4) reflect God's providence in Israel’s territorial boundaries?
options: It shows God’s providential care in establishing physical limits for the people
It indicates God’s wrath by limiting Israel’s expansion
It reveals God’s indifference to territorial matters
It demonstrates God’s condemnation of neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s providential care in establishing physical limits for the people
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:4 sets the south border toward the river of Egypt and the sea, illustrating God’s providence in defining Israel’s boundaries, which ensured protection and order (Psalm 147:19-20).

questions.question: According to Joshua 15:5, what theological truth is taught about God's sovereign control over geographical boundaries?
options: God ordains boundaries even of seas and rivers
God is limited by natural borders
God allows humans to create boundaries arbitrarily
God’s sovereignty is only spiritual, not territorial
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains boundaries even of seas and rivers
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:5 states the east border was the salt sea unto the end of Jordan, indicating God’s sovereign authority over all creation including natural features that define human boundaries (Acts 17:26).

questions.question: What does the mention of the 'stone of Bohan the son of Reuben' in Joshua 15:6 symbolize in a broader theological context?
options: God’s faithfulness to His covenant with all tribes
The fall of the tribe of Reuben
The rejection of the tribe of Judah
The establishment of a new covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to His covenant with all tribes
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:6 references the stone of Bohan, son of Reuben, showing that God’s promises and boundaries encompass all tribes, affirming His faithfulness to His covenant with Israel (Genesis 49:1).

questions.question: How does the border description including Jerusalem and the valley of Hinnom (Joshua 15:8) fit within the redemptive narrative of Scripture?
options: Jerusalem as God’s chosen city foreshadows Christ’s kingdom
It shows the failure of Israel to conquer Canaan
It represents the exile of Judah
It signifies the destruction of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Jerusalem as God’s chosen city foreshadows Christ’s kingdom
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:8 includes Jerusalem within Judah’s border, highlighting the city’s central role as God’s chosen place, which in the New Testament becomes the spiritual center of Christ’s kingdom (Psalm 48:1-2; Revelation 21:2).

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by Caleb’s faithful conquest and inheritance of Hebron as recorded in Joshua 15:13-14?
options: The doctrine of sanctification through faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of sanctification through faithfulness
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:13-14 shows Caleb’s conquest and possession of Hebron as a reward for faithfulness, illustrating sanctification as a process of being set apart and blessed through obedience (Hebrews 11:6).

questions.question: What theological significance can be derived from Achsah’s request for springs of water in Joshua 15:19?
options: It symbolizes the believer’s need for spiritual refreshment
It shows a disregard for God’s provision
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the believer’s need for spiritual refreshment
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:19 records Achsah asking for springs of water, which can typologically represent the believer’s desire for spiritual nourishment and living water provided by God (John 4:14).

questions.question: Which combined doctrinal insight do verses 15:20 and 15:21-62 provide about God's covenantal promise and the inheritance of His people?
options: God faithfully fulfills His covenant promises by allotting specific inheritances
God’s promises are conditional and often unfulfilled
Inheritance is based on human strength alone
God’s covenant is only spiritual, not physical
questions.correctAnswer: God faithfully fulfills His covenant promises by allotting specific inheritances
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:20 and 15:21-62 list the cities and lands given to Judah, demonstrating God’s faithfulness in fulfilling His covenant promises of inheritance to His people (Genesis 17:8).

questions.question: How does the inability of the children of Judah to drive out the Jebusites from Jerusalem (Joshua 15:63) illustrate a theological truth about human weakness and divine sovereignty?
options: It shows human limitations despite divine promises, emphasizing dependence on God
It means God’s promises are unreliable
It indicates the Jebusites were more righteous
It reflects God’s rejection of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: It shows human limitations despite divine promises, emphasizing dependence on God
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:63 reveals that Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, highlighting human weakness and the need for God’s sovereign intervention to fully possess the promised land (Judges 1:21).

questions.question: What combined teaching about God’s providential ordering and human responsibility is conveyed by Joshua 15:16-17 alongside 15:19?
options: God’s providence works through human faithfulness and initiative
God acts independently of human action
Human effort is irrelevant to God’s plans
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence works through human faithfulness and initiative
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:16-17 and 15:19 show Caleb’s promise to give his daughter Achsah in marriage to whoever conquers Kirjathsepher and her subsequent request for water, illustrating how God’s providence includes human faithfulness and initiative (Philippians 2:12-13).

questions.question: Which doctrine is most clearly taught by the extensive list of cities given to Judah in Joshua 15:21-62?
options: The doctrine of God’s covenant faithfulness in physical blessings
The doctrine of justification by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God’s covenant faithfulness in physical blessings
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:21-62 enumerates the cities allotted to Judah, reflecting God’s covenant faithfulness by providing tangible blessings and inheritance to His people (Deuteronomy 7:13).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the detailed territorial allotments in Joshua 15 show human invention rather than divine inspiration. What does Joshua 15:1-12 actually teach about God’s role in Israel’s settlement?
options: God sovereignly directs the boundaries and allotments given to His people
The boundaries were arbitrarily chosen by human leaders
The land was divided randomly without divine guidance
The allotments were symbolic only and never physically realized
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly directs the boundaries and allotments given to His people
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:1-12 outlines precise boundaries given to Judah by lot, indicating divine sovereign direction in Israel’s settlement (Numbers 26:52-56), countering sceptical claims of human invention.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed through His giving of the city of Hebron to Caleb (Joshua 15:13)?
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:13 shows God giving Hebron to Caleb as a reward for his faith and obedience, revealing God’s faithfulness in blessing those who follow His commands (Hebrews 6:10).

questions.question: How do verses Joshua 15:8 and 15:63 together contribute to the understanding of God’s justice and human disobedience in the conquest of Canaan?
options: They show God’s justice allows consequences for incomplete obedience
They indicate God’s partiality to some tribes
They demonstrate God’s forgiveness without conditions
They reveal that God abandons His people when they fail
questions.correctAnswer: They show God’s justice allows consequences for incomplete obedience
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:8 includes Jerusalem within Judah’s borders, but 15:63 states Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, teaching that incomplete obedience leads to consequences under God’s just governance (Numbers 32:23).

questions.question: What theological insight about human vocation and divine blessing is given by Caleb’s challenge and reward in Joshua 15:16-17?
options: God blesses courageous and faithful human action
God’s blessings are arbitrary and unearned
Human effort is unnecessary for divine blessing
Blessings come only through ritual observance
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses courageous and faithful human action
questions.explanation: Joshua 15:16-17 shows Caleb offering his daughter Achsah as a reward for conquering a city, illustrating that God honors human courage and faithfulness with blessing (2 Timothy 2:12).
